visualizerParams.title: Bug Squasher: Screen reader never hears the state
visualizerParams.problemDescription: The button text changes between Mute and Unmute, but a screen reader always announces it as not pressed. The script updates the words and forgets the aria-pressed attribute.
visualizerParams.buggyCode:
<button id="m" aria-pressed="false">Mute</button>
<script>
  var m = document.getElementById('m');
  m.addEventListener('click', function () {
    var on = m.getAttribute('aria-pressed') !== 'true';
    m.textContent = on ? 'Unmute' : 'Mute';
  });
</script>

solution.code:
<button id="m" aria-pressed="false">Mute</button>
<script>
  var m = document.getElementById('m');
  m.addEventListener('click', function () {
    var on = m.getAttribute('aria-pressed') !== 'true';
    m.setAttribute('aria-pressed', on);
    m.textContent = on ? 'Unmute' : 'Mute';
  });
</script>
solution.explanation: Visible text is only half of the interface. A screen reader reads aria-pressed to say whether a toggle button is on, so the script must update it every time the state changes.

checks.label: The attribute says pressed after the click
